meaning: `=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff` names this Mac's Bluetooth address when the Mac's Bluetooth host controller does not give it (IOBluetooth): a paired Switch 2 controller wakes with an advertisement addressed to it, and pairing gives it this address

name: DM_SW2_MAP
meaning: `=a,b,c,d,e,f` replaces the built-in map from a Switch 2 controller's raw sensor channels (1 to 6: accelerometer x y z, gyro x y z, a minus flips the sign) to the Switch frame's acceleration x y z and rotation x y z, e.g. `-1,-2,-3,4,5,6` for a Joy-Con 2 held upright

name: DM_SW2_MOTION
meaning: `=0` leaves out the motion of Switch 2 controllers (buttons, sticks and rumble stay)

name: DM_SW2_MOTION_SIDE
meaning: `=L` takes a Joy-Con 2 pair's motion from the left Joy-Con instead of the right one

name: DM_SW2_VERBOSE
meaning: `=1` logs the first report of each second of every Switch 2 controller: buttons, sticks, raw sensors, battery

name: DM_SYMCHECK
meaning: `=1` checks every hashed module symbol lookup against a linear search and logs a red line for each mismatch

name: DM_TARGET
meaning: `android` makes `patch_nso.py` rewrite the thread-slot reads for Android (`mov xN, x18`) instead of Apple's; the Android packing script sets it

name: DM_TBUF_ALIGN
meaning: `=<bytes>` uses that value as the linear-texture alignment when it is larger than the device's `minimumLinearTextureAlignmentForPixelFormat`, for buffer textures and for linear textures on a pool's buffer: a Mac can then reproduce a phone's larger alignment (a 64-byte one fails the buffers and linear textures a device with 64 bytes cannot view), to check `tbuf_as_2d`'s aligned-row copy and the upload of unaligned linear textures (`linear_fit`)

name: DM_TEAM_ID
meaning: Apple team ID for the per-game Xcode project, used when `--team-id` / `TEAM_ID` is not given; `build_ipa.sh` uses the placeholder `0000000000` (unsigned) when unset

name: DM_TEMP
meaning: Temporary storage folder (default `$DM_ROOT/run/platform/temp`); stand-in system data goes in `<DM_TEMP>_sysdata`; the Mac launcher, the iOS app and the NSP script set it

name: DM_TEST_ARCHIVE_CONSTANTS
meaning: Use optional function constants in the synthetic pipeline archive restart fixture

name: DM_TEST_ARCHIVE_MIXED
meaning: Mix a newly compiled shader function with compacted bases in the archive restart fixture

name: DM_TEST_BORDER
meaning: Path to the native t_border executable that test_dmsh_border.py runs a rewritten shader through on the GPU (`make check_t_border` sets it)

name: DM_TEST_BUILD
meaning: Build folder of `dm/host/tests` whose `t_svc_memory` `test_memory_profile.py` runs (default `build`; `make asan` sets `build/asan`)

name: DM_TEST_FS_FAIL
meaning: `=write:<n>[:<errno>]` makes the nth save write fail with that errno (default ENOSPC), which refuses the save transaction's commit

name: DM_TEST_FS_FAILAT
meaning: `=<point>[:<count>][,…]` makes steps of the save transaction (`mountclone`, `reclone`, `guestname`, `renameback`) fail with ENOSPC

name: DM_TEST_GEOMETRY
meaning: Path of the native `t_geometry` executable; `test_dmsh_geometry.py` runs its native geometry emitter checks only when it is set

name: DM_TEST_GEOMETRY_PRIMITIVE_ID
meaning: Path to the native t_geometry_primitive_id replay executable used by test_dmsh_geometry.py with DMSH_TEST_GPU=1.

name: DM_TEST_GPU_LOST
meaning: `=<n>` imitates the GPU access macOS revoked from the nth submission on: each submission's feedback reports `MTL4CommandQueueErrorAccessRevoked` and the GPU does not signal its fence, so the host stops presenting and the front end ends the game

name: DM_TEST_KEYRACE
meaning: `=<n>` creates up to n (at most 512) pthread keys on a thread of its own while the host starts up

name: DM_TEST_KILL_AT
meaning: `=write:<n>` exits the process (`_exit(9)`) at the nth save write, imitating a kill mid-write

name: DM_TEST_LEAK_GPU
meaning: `=1` allocates and keeps a 1 MB shared Metal buffer every 100 ticks: a GPU memory leak on demand

name: DM_TEST_LINK_STALL
meaning: `=<start s>,<duration s>`: counting from the first present, pauses the display link at that point for that long, to check the present fallback

name: DM_TEST_NO_METAL4
meaning: `=1` treats the GPU as one without Metal 4, as on a virtual Mac: the NVN layer starts only its classic part and drops every present

name: DM_TEST_PRESENT_LAG
meaning: `=<every n>,<ms>[,<in a row>][;…]` sleeps that long before every nth present (and the ones after it in the run): a slow frame on demand

name: DM_TEST_SWKBD_HOLD_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (with `DM_KBD`) keeps the system keyboard up that long before `DM_KBD`'s text is returned, as a player typing would

name: DM_TEST_SWKBD_LAG_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` sleeps that long between the keyboard handing back its text and the game's thread getting the result, to check that auto-accept does not act early

name: DM_TEST_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK
meaning: Path to the native t_transform_feedback executable used by the Python feedback tests

name: DM_TEST_UP_LEAK
meaning: `=1` keeps the old upload staging block instead of retiring it, as before the fix, to measure the leak

name: DM_TEST_UP_LOST
meaning: `=<batch index>` treats that batch of uploads as dropped, to exercise the re-upload path

name: DM_TEXT_TEST
meaning: Android: `1` shows the software keyboard's text box once after the demo, `2` also types and confirms in it (`front_android.c`, `Gamepad.java`)

name: DM_THERMAL_CAP
meaning: `0` turns off the thermal cap, which holds the frame step at 30 fps while iOS reports a serious or critical thermal state (on by default)

name: DM_THR
meaning: `=1` logs each SVC (except `SleepThread`) with its first four arguments, and each `CreateThread` with entry, stack, priority and core

name: DM_THRCPU
meaning: `=<tsv path>[,<seconds>]` writes each thread's CPU time (100% = one core) and the total every interval (default 10 s); on iOS a relative path is under `Documents`

name: DM_TOUCH_HAPTICS
meaning: `0` turns off the light haptic tap when a touch control is pressed (on by default); launcher setting

name: DM_TOUCH_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs each touch-screen read with touch points (sample, finger, position, attributes) and each gesture entry, up to 500 lines

name: DM_UDC_SELFTEST
meaning: `=1` runs a start-up check of DontCare load and store on private depth-stencil and RGBA8 textures (clear, Load + DontCare, read back) and logs one result line

name: DM_UE_DECODE
meaning: `phone`: `build_android_from_nsp.py` decodes with the game's Oodle on the phone (`scripts/android_oodle.py`) even where a Mac build beside the NSP folder could: an Unreal game's shaders though that build holds decoded archives made from the same files, and the streams of Oodle-compressed archives (`oodle_packs`) though its Mac host could decode them (a test of the phone's decode on a Mac)

name: DM_UE_SHADERS
meaning: Folder of the Unreal shader code archives decoded by `uepak.py`, for `shader_split.py` (default `ue_shaders` beside the RomFS); needed when the RomFS has Unreal paks

name: DM_UE_TEXTURE_POOL
meaning: Megabytes Unreal's texture streaming pool (`r.Streaming.PoolSize`) is raised to, overriding the profile's `ue_texture_pool`; `0` keeps the game's own pool. On iOS only this switch turns it on (`Documents/env.txt`)

name: DM_UE_DYNRES_BUDGET
meaning: Milliseconds Unreal's dynamic resolution aims for (`r.DynamicRes.FrameTimeBudget`): the default 33.3 is the Switch's 30 fps, so a host that could present 60 scales the internal size instead; `16.7` aims at 60 fps; `0` or unset keeps the game's own budget

name: DM_UPSCALER
meaning: `metalfx` draws the game's own upscaler shaders (agl's NDSR network, found by the shader map) with MetalFX's spatial scaler; `game` (the default) runs them

name: DM_VK_ADPF
meaning: Android: `0` makes no performance hint session (APerformanceHint, Android 13), so the frame's deadline (the time-constraint declaration's period) reaches no one and the present thread's declaration fails as before; on by default, each present reports the frame's work (`plat_android.c`, `gfx_vk.c` `hint_frame`)

name: DM_VK_ADPF_DONE
meaning: Android: `0` leaves the replay's completion thread (`vk-done`) out of the performance hint session (in by default)

name: DM_VK_ADPF_HOLD
meaning: Android: `0` sets the performance hint session's target to the declared period whatever the frame step's hold (`rt_period_ns`, the cap's while the hold is raised); on by default, under the frame step the target is the cost its fit trial needs to try the next hold down, `FSTEP_FIT` × max(kmin, k − 1) vsyncs (`gfx_vk.c` `hint_frame`)

name: DM_VK_ADPF_LOG
meaning: Android: `=1` logs the frame work reported to the performance hint session every 300 presents (mean, max, frames over the target) and each change of the session's target

name: DM_VK_ADPF_THERMAL
meaning: Android: `0` keeps the performance hint session through thermal mitigation; on by default, the session is closed while the thermal state is serious or worse or the frame step's thermal cap holds 30 fps, and made again after 60 presents with neither (`plat_android.c` `dm_android_hint_frame`)

name: DM_VK_ALIAS
meaning: Android: `0` gives each of a shader's bindings of the same guest memory a copy and a write-back of its own, as before; by default, a binding inside a write-back the same draw or dispatch made for another binding is bound on that copy (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `own_alias`, `dm/android/wb_alias.h`), as the two views are one buffer on the Switch

name: DM_VK_ASYNC_DELAY_MS
meaning: Android: `=<ms>` makes each background pipeline build wait that long first, which shows what a slow driver's builds leave out (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `apipe_thread`)

name: DM_VK_ASYNC_EQUAL
meaning: Android: `1` leaves draws that test depth EQUAL without writing it out while their new pipeline builds, as before droidplay-core#444 (by default they build at once: left out, the clear colour shows through the pre-pass's depth; `apipe_rule.h`)

name: DM_VK_ASYNC_PIPE
meaning: Android: `0` builds every pipeline met for the first time at once, on the replay thread; by default one whose pass's targets are drawn every frame builds in the background and its draw is left out meanwhile (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `apipe_ok`)

name: DM_VK_BC
meaning: Android: `1` puts GPU breadcrumbs around every dispatch (`gfx_vk_bc.inc`): the GPU writes the dispatch's number into a host-visible ring before it and again after it, and the host keeps its shader, groups and bindings (uniform and storage buffers with their first words, textures and images with serial, size and format). A slow submission (`gpu_slow`) then lists its dispatches that never ended, and a lost device the last eight begun and never ended, with their bindings; see [A GPU hang names the dispatch it was in](reference/rendering.md#a-gpu-hang-names-the-dispatch-it-was-in-with-its-bindings). Each dispatch waits for the one before, so frame times with it on are not the game's; off with `DM_VK_RECORDER=1`

name: DM_VK_BC_GPU_DECODE
meaning: Android, on a GPU without BC textures: a GPU block encoder's pass into a BC4 or BC5 texture that the CPU decoded draws into a block shadow, and the shadow's blocks are decoded into the image on the GPU after the pass (on by default; `0` draws into the decoded image, as before; `gfx_vk_bcdec.inc` `bcd_decode`)

name: DM_VK_BIND_COMPACT
meaning: Android: `0` keeps a shader set's binding numbers as the translator gave them. By default each binding at 1024 or past it (Ocarina of Time's constant buffers at 1,048,576 and up) gets a dense number past the set's others, in the module and in the layout alike (`spv_bind.h`), since Samsung's Xclipse driver keeps 64 bytes per binding number up to a layout's highest; see [Set layouts sized by their highest binding number](reference/rendering.md#set-layouts-sized-by-their-highest-binding-number)

name: DM_VK_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<dir>` (Mac) writes every SPIR-V module the game creates to `<dir>/<key>.spv`; the NSP script's Vulkan shader capture stage sets it

name: DM_VK_CB_EXT2
meaning: Android: `0` finds how much of each constant buffer a shader reads with the old word match (`spv_cb_ext`, any word equal to the variable's id keeps the whole buffer); on by default, by operand (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `spv_cb_ext2`)

name: DM_VK_CHUNKS
meaning: Android: `=<2-16>` how many chunks of commands the Vulkan replay keeps in use at once, the one being recorded and those on the GPU (default 8, 4 before); each keeps the arena blocks and descriptor sets it has used, so more cost memory

name: DM_VK_COPIED_DEPTH
meaning: Android: the first render pass on a depth image after a copy into it begins with a depth-writing draw (compare `ALWAYS`) of no pixels, so Qualcomm's driver forgets the image's low-resolution depth, which a copy leaves stale (on by default on Qualcomm's own driver, by its Vulkan driver ID, so not on Turnip; Skyrim's first-person model drew as the clear colour on an Adreno 740 without it, droidplay-core#444; `0` off, `1` on any driver; `gfx_vk_dscopy.inc` `copied_depth_pass`)

name: DM_VK_CS_BARRIER
meaning: Android: `full` records a full pipeline barrier before and after every compute dispatch, as before (diagnostic); by default a dispatch that follows another gets a barrier only when the game issued one between them, and a run of dispatches gets its barrier before the next command of another kind (`gfx_vk.c` `cs_game`, the rule of seedds/nxnative 547c5db6)

name: DM_VK_DEBUG
meaning: Android: logs every shader and pipeline the Vulkan replay makes (`gfx_vk_draw.inc`)

name: DM_VK_DRIVER
meaning: Android, on an Adreno GPU: `=<file>` runs that Vulkan driver (a Turnip build's `.so`) instead of the system's, named relative to the folder `env.txt` is in or by an absolute path; copied into the app's internal files and opened through libadrenotools (`dm/android/vk_driver.c`). A driver that can't be opened, offers no GPU, fails to make the device, or fails the first window's surface or swapchain (the device is then made again in the same process) gets one `[RED] [vk] DM_VK_DRIVER` line and the system's driver runs; after a start that crashed in the driver's code, lost the GPU or ended in its first 30 s, the next start runs the system's driver once (`vk_driver_state/<driver file>.json`, `games/<title ID>/vk_driver_result.txt`); a phone without `/dev/kgsl-3d0` (Mali, Xclipse) ignores it

name: DM_VK_DRIVER_FAIL
meaning: Android: `=<step>` makes that step fail while a `DM_VK_DRIVER` driver runs, as if the driver had failed it, to try the fallback to the system's driver on a phone whose driver works: `instance`, `gpu`, `queue`, `extensions` (the window surface and swapchain) or `device` (`gfx_vk.c` `vk_try`), or `swapchain` (the first window's, `front_android.c` `vk_window_first`); `crash` crashes the game in the driver's code at the replay's first use of the device, to try the crash guard (`vk_driver.c` `crash_hook`), and `crash_host` crashes in the host's code there (recorded as `crashed elsewhere`, which doesn't skip the driver)

name: DM_VK_DUMP
meaning: Android: `=<frame>` dumps every pass's colour targets of that frame to `DM_DUMP_DIR` with a per-draw log (`files/dump_now` asks for the next frame)

name: DM_VK_DUP_SLOTS
meaning: Android: an image that two colour slots of a render pass name is attached once, at the first slot the pass's first draw writes (else the first), the other slots left unused (on by default; Vulkan leaves aliasing attachments undefined, and the Adreno 830 stored an unwritten copy over the written one; `0` attaches it at every slot, as before; `gfx_vk_draw.inc` `dup_slots`)

name: DM_VK_E5_STORE
meaning: Android: `0` skips a compute dispatch that binds an E5B9G9R9 texture to an image slot, as before; by default the texture is stored through an R32_UINT view and the shader packs RGB9E5 (`dm/android/spv_e5.h`)

name: DM_VK_EXT_CHECK
meaning: Android: `=1` copies and binds each constant buffer whole with NaN past the extent the shader is said to read (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `cb_ext_pick`), so an extent too small shows as a broken picture

name: DM_VK_FP_HOST
meaning: Android: `0` lets the driver compile shaders and pipelines with the calling thread's FPCR, as before (the game's flush-to-zero, which made Ocarina of Time far too bright on Qualcomm's driver); by default the calls that compile run with FPCR 0 (`dm/android/vk_driver.c`), and the pipeline cache file is `pipeline.cache.fp0`

name: DM_VK_GC_EVICT_PACE
meaning: Android: `0` walks the geometry cache's whole table for copies to let go at every request that finds no room, as before; by default the walk is made at most once a present, and after one that freed nothing only every 60th (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `gc_evict`)

name: DM_VK_GPU_FLOOR
meaning: Android, Qualcomm's kernel GPU driver (KGSL): `=100` (the launcher's Keep the GPU clock up, offered for every game on a phone with `/dev/kgsl-3d0`, off by default) holds the GPU at its highest clock through a power constraint on the Vulkan device's own KGSL contexts; `=2..99` a floor at that share of it where the GMU decides the clock (the highest clock where the kernel does); `0` or unset sends nothing. The log says once whether it was taken. Faster where the governor keeps the GPU slow and the phone has thermal headroom (Ocarina of Time on a cool Galaxy Z Fold 8), no faster on others (a Galaxy S25 Edge), slower on a warm phone whose thermal engine then limits the GPU harder (the same Fold), warmer everywhere (`gfx_vk_floor.inc`, `gpu_floor.h`; after Banana Native's vka_dev.c)

name: DM_VK_HARR
meaning: Android: `0` keeps a shader's texture, sampler and image arrays as long as the translator declared them, as before. By default an array longer than the 1,024 elements the replay writes (a handle array from a uniform buffer is 8,192: 64 KB of handles) is shortened to 1,024 when its module is made, its indices clamped again, and the set layout holds 1,024 descriptors for it: each of Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door's reflection sets held 8,192, two of them filled a 12.4 MB descriptor pool, and the pools reached 6.7 GB in the prologue (`spv_harr.h`, `gfx_vk_draw.inc` `spv_fit_harr`)

name: DM_VK_IMAGE_EVICT
meaning: Android: `0` keeps every texture's image until another description takes over its storage with no object left on it, or its memory pool is finalized, as before; by default two kinds go (`gfx_vk_evict.inc`): a shared image that another one over at least half its storage was written as since its last lookup, after `DM_VK_IMAGE_EVICT_ALIAS_AGE` presents without one (the console overwrote that memory too), and an image whose content is still in guest memory (a packaged texture, or a shared one filled from its storage) that the GPU never wrote and the texture pool by ID never read, after `DM_VK_IMAGE_EVICT_AGE` presents without a lookup. The next lookup makes either again

name: DM_VK_IMAGE_EVICT_AGE
meaning: Android: `=<presents>`: how long an image whose content is still in guest memory goes without a lookup before `DM_VK_IMAGE_EVICT` evicts it (default 600, about 20 s at 30 fps) (`gfx_vk_evict.inc`)

name: DM_VK_IMAGE_EVICT_ALIAS_AGE
meaning: Android: `=<presents>`: how long a shared image another one overwrote goes without a lookup before `DM_VK_IMAGE_EVICT` evicts it (default 30, about a second at 30 fps) (`gfx_vk_evict.inc`)

name: DM_VK_IMAGE_EVICT_LOG
meaning: Android: `1` logs a line at each image eviction scan (every 30 presents): the images alive and how many it chose (`gfx_vk_evict.inc`); the memory line every 300 frames has the totals either way

name: DM_VK_IMAGE_SPARE
meaning: Android: `0` frees an image's memory with the image, as before. By default a freed image's memory (256 KiB or more) is kept as a spare once the chunks that may use it complete, and a new image takes the smallest spare of a memory type it allows that holds it with at most a quarter to spare instead of calling vkAllocateMemory; spares unused for 120 presents, and the oldest while over `DM_VK_IMAGE_SPARE_MB`, are freed. The memory line every 300 frames gives the image allocations and their time, and the spares taken, kept and let go (`gfx_vk_spare.inc`, `img_spare.h`; the idea of nx2android's e3b16fdf)

name: DM_VK_IMAGE_SPARE_MB
meaning: Android: `=<MB>`: the most memory `DM_VK_IMAGE_SPARE` keeps in spares (default 256) (`gfx_vk_spare.inc`)

name: DM_VK_INPLACE
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `0` copies a storage buffer a shader only reads into the arena and compares it at every draw, as before, even when it lies in a placed pool; by default such a buffer is bound as the pool piece's own buffer at its offset (`dm/android/gfx_vk_gmem_inplace.inc`)

name: DM_VK_INPLACE_WRITE
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `0` copies a storage buffer a shader writes into the arena with a snapshot and writes it back when its submission completes, as before, even when it lies in a placed pool; by default it is bound in place and its pages are only marked written when the submission completes

name: DM_VK_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs Vulkan object creation in the Vulkan-on-Metal layer

name: DM_VK_MESH
meaning: Android: `0` doesn't use VK_EXT_mesh_shader, so task / mesh draws run in compute form (or are skipped with `DM_VK_MESH_EMU=0`); `1` uses it on Qualcomm's driver too, where they run in compute form by default because the native path draws Ocarina of Time's foliage torn

name: DM_VK_MESH_ARENA_MB
meaning: Android, without VK_EXT_mesh_shader: the megabytes of GPU memory the compute form of task / mesh draws writes its outputs to (default 64; a draw larger than it goes in parts; `gfx_vk_meshemu.inc`)

name: DM_VK_MESH_EMU
meaning: Android: `0` skips NVN2 task / mesh draws on a GPU without VK_EXT_mesh_shader, as before; by default they run in compute form, the task and mesh kernels as compute dispatches and an indexed draw (`gfx_vk_meshemu.inc`, `spv_meshemu.py`)

name: DM_VK_MESH_LEAVE_OUT
meaning: Android: `=1` (the launcher's Fewer plants, offered for a game whose android_defaults.txt carries the key) leaves out the task / mesh draws whose mesh shader is one of the game profile's `mesh_leave_out` keys, `=<key>[,<key>...]` names keys itself; a draw whose stage writes guest memory still runs (the compute producers and their readers stay). A picture trade, off by default: Ocarina of Time's ferns, flowers and tree canopies for about 3 ms of a phone's GPU frame (`gfx_vk_mesh.inc` mesh_left_out; the list and the idea are nebadasSwifty's, Banana Native #167)

name: DM_VK_MESH_MAX
meaning: Android, without VK_EXT_mesh_shader: the most mesh workgroups a part of a task / mesh draw in compute form launches (default 4096, fewer when the arena holds fewer; a task's launches past it are dropped; `gfx_vk_meshemu.inc`)

name: DM_VK_MID_DRAWS
meaning: Android: `=<n>` sends a chunk to the GPU after that many draws in the middle of a pass (default 64; the pass is begun again with its targets loaded); Breath of the Wild's `android_defaults.txt` sets 512 (`gfx_vk.c` `mid_poll`; a `vk_mid` file beside `DM_DUMP_DIR` still changes it during a run)

name: DM_VK_MODULE_ID
meaning: Android: `0` makes every shader module as its shader loads (as before); on by default where the GPU has `VK_EXT_shader_module_identifier` and pipeline creation cache control, a module is only its identifier until a pipeline the driver's cache does not have needs it, and pipelines are asked for from the identifiers first (`gfx_vk_lmod.inc`)

name: DM_VK_N16_HALF
meaning: Android: `0` makes 16-bit normalized colour textures (R16, R16G16, R16G16B16A16, UNORM and SNORM) in their own formats, as before; by default, on a GPU that cannot filter such a format linearly but can filter the 16-bit float format of the same channels (the Xclipse 950), a sampled one that is not a storage image is made in the float format, its texels converted on upload and on CPU reads (`gfx_vk.c` `n16_half`)

name: DM_VK_NDVE
meaning: Android: `1` runs `nn::ndve`'s movie network (Ocarina of Time's title and opening movies), all 22 compute shaders of `Movie/Ndve/Ndve-Nvn2-vid_seq5.dat`, which the Vulkan replay leaves out by default (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `ndve_left_out`): Qualcomm's compiler does not finish its largest U-Net shader, and without the U-Net the rest cost up to 1.2 s a frame on an Adreno 740 for a movie picture that stays black; see [The NDVE movie network left out on Vulkan](reference/shaders.md#the-ndve-movie-network-left-out-on-vulkan)

name: DM_VK_OCCLUSION
meaning: Android: what a draw stretch between a counter reset and its samples-passed report records (`gfx_vk.c` `occl_mode`): `precise` (the default) an occlusion query with the precise count where the GPU offers it, as before; `any` one without it, whose result is zero when no sample passed and otherwise nonzero, which is all a condition's equality needs; `0` no query at all, every stretch counting as one sample passed and every condition drawing (Ocarina of Time's `android_defaults.txt`: its queries cost more than the culling saved on an Adreno 830)

name: DM_VK_POOL
meaning: Android: `0` leaves NVN2's texture and sampler pools read by ID (Ryujinx's handle fallback, `<stage>_t_cb0_40000000`) off, and the draws of the shaders that read them are dropped, as before; by default they read the replay's pool set, which holds the textures the shaders were seen reading (`dm/android/gfx_vk_pool.inc`, `spv_pool.h`)

name: DM_VK_PROF_TOP
meaning: Android: `=<n>` makes a `prof_now` frame's profile (`[prof]` lines, costliest record first) stop after n records; every record is listed by default. A pass begun again on the same framebuffer after a chunk was sent in its middle is marked `(piece)`, the pieces' total is in the frame line, and `whole pass` lines sum each pass with its pieces

name: DM_VK_POOL_FILEBACK
meaning: Android: `auto` (the texture kind on a phone under 14 GiB of RAM; Ocarina of Time's default), `texture`, `shader` or `shader,texture` (`all`): memory pools of that kind are backed by one unlinked file in `DM_TEMP` from their Initialize, so what the game keeps in them is a clean page the kernel drops and reads back, not compressed swap: texture = any pool of at least `DM_VK_POOL_FILEBACK_MB` not compressible, physical or virtual (Ocarina of Time's texture pools), shader = shader code. Writers are held for the copy; a range raw global memory places is cut out of the file, and a pool's Finalize gives its pieces back to anonymous memory. Off by default; the memory line gives the pools, MiB backed and written to storage (`gfx_vk_fileback.inc`, `pool_fileback.h`; BananaNative's RAM saver, DM_MEM_FILEBACK_KINDS)

name: DM_VK_POOL_FILEBACK_MB
meaning: Android: `=<MiB>`: the smallest pool `DM_VK_POOL_FILEBACK`'s texture kind backs (default 64) (`gfx_vk_fileback.inc`)

name: DM_VK_POOL_LOG
meaning: Android: `1` logs each texture-pool ID the first time a shader reads it, with the texture registered there and the view made (`gfx_vk_pool.inc` `pool_sync`)

name: DM_VK_POS_ROWS
meaning: Android: `1` makes every vertex shader's position read its constant buffer rows at run time (`spv_android.py` `pos_rows`, the specialization constant `gfx_vk_posrows.inc` sets), on any GPU, to look for other draws Qualcomm's Adreno 7xx driver loses in its binning copy of a vertex shader; `0` in none. By default only the vertex shaders the game's profile names (`vk_pos_rows`), and only on Qualcomm's Adreno 7xx driver: on in every vertex shader, run-time rows cost GPU time (Animal Crossing's island +25% on the Odin 2)

name: DM_VK_PRESENT_TIMING
meaning: Android: `0` paces frames on the host's own clock and shows each as soon as drawn (as before); by default, where a frame spans a whole number of refreshes (2 or more), each frame starts just past a vsync the swapchain reported and is shown at a set time (`VK_GOOGLE_display_timing`, `gfx_vk_vsync.inc`), so its work can no longer cross a latch early or late

name: DM_VK_PREWARM
meaning: Android: how many pipelines of the list the replay makes again at start (default 3000; `0` none)

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM
meaning: Android: `1` (a game's `android_defaults.txt`, or `env.txt`) gives NVN2 shaders' raw global memory (loads and stores at addresses read from memory, through the raw pool table under constant buffer slot 0xFF) the real memory pools: each pool the game takes a buffer address in becomes Vulkan memory at its own address, with a device address, and the table lists them; storage buffers in those pools are bound there (`DM_VK_INPLACE`). Off by default, and the device is then made without its extensions. Needs a Qualcomm Adreno or a Samsung Xclipse (`DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_ANYGPU=1` tries another GPU) with `VK_KHR_buffer_device_address` and either `VK_EXT_map_memory_placed` or AHardwareBuffer import (`dm/android/gfx_vk_gmem.inc`)

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_AHB
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `1` places the memory pools as AHardwareBuffers mapped over their pages and imported into Vulkan even on a GPU that has `VK_EXT_map_memory_placed` (the route a GPU without it takes)

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_ANYGPU
meaning: Android, with `DM_VK_RAW_GMEM=1`: `1` tries raw global memory on a GPU other than Qualcomm's Adreno and Samsung's Xclipse (Mali would take the AHardwareBuffer route, untested there); by default it stays off there, with a red line

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_CHECK
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `1` logs the 64-bit words at the start of the storage buffers that shaders binding the raw pool table read, which look like guest addresses, each with where it lies (a placed pool, a pool not placed, none) and the bytes there

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_CODE
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `1` places shader-code memory pools as other pools; by default they are left out (the replay runs translated shaders, and no raw pointer reaches shader code), which keeps Ocarina of Time's 345 MiB of them swappable

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_LAZY
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `0` places a memory pool whole at its first buffer address, as before; by default every pool is placed in 2 MiB chunks (one under 2 MiB as a single chunk), each when a storage buffer in it is bound or a pointer in a raw-memory shader's storage buffers reaches it (`dm/android/gfx_vk_gmem_lazy.inc`), so pages nothing on the GPU reaches are not committed

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_LAZY_MIN
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on and chunked placement: `=<bytes>` (or whole K / M / G) places the memory pools under that size whole at their first buffer address, as the first chunked version did with 4M; by default every pool is chunked

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_MAX
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `=<bytes>` (or whole K / M / G) caps the memory pools placed as Vulkan memory (default a quarter of the device's memory: placed memory is committed whole); a pool past the cap stays anonymous and is copied as before, and raw accesses to it read 0

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_NOPTR
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `1` reaches the placed pools through a storage-buffer array (a set of its own, a slot per piece, the table's deltas the slots) and rewrites the shaders' physical pointers into accesses to it (`spv_noptr.h`) without first building the probe pipeline; `0` never does. By default the array is used only when the driver refuses the probe's `OpConvertUToPtr` (the Ayn Odin 2's Adreno 740 V@0676.32, the Razr's 730) on a device that has runtime descriptor arrays, non-uniform storage-buffer indexing and update-after-bind storage buffers

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_NOPTR_NU
meaning: Android, with raw global memory through the pools' array (`DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_NOPTR`): `0` leaves the `NonUniform` decorations off the array's accesses, to tell what a driver's non-uniform indexing costs; wrong where the lanes of one draw reach different pieces. On the Razr's Adreno 730 it changed nothing in Frostpunk's GPU time

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_NOPTR_SET
meaning: Android, with raw global memory through the pools' array: `3` puts the array at descriptor set 3 on a GPU that binds 6 sets at once (where it is at set 5), to try what a GPU that binds only 4 or 5 gets

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_NOPTR_SLOTS
meaning: Android, with raw global memory through the pools' array: `=<n>` makes the array at most n slots long (default: the table's 8,192, or what the GPU's update-after-bind limits allow), to tell what its length costs; pieces past it are not reached. On the Razr's Adreno 730, 16 slots changed nothing in Frostpunk's GPU time

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_REACHED
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on and chunked placement: `0` places only the two chunks at each pointer a scan finds; by default a pool a pointer reaches also gets the chunks the CPU wrote in it placed, every 200 ms (a shader may index far into a pool from one pointer)

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_SINK
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `1` puts every chunk not placed into the raw pool table, onto one zeroed 2 MiB sink, so raw stores into such chunks are counted (their write logs) and the first named in a red line; raw loads from them then read the sink

name: DM_VK_IND_FWD
meaning: Android: `1` (Ocarina of Time's and Mario Kart World's android_defaults.txt) makes an indirect dispatch whose arguments the GPU wrote earlier run as vkCmdDispatchIndirect on the write's GPU copy, its counts copied into its c0 bank on the GPU, instead of waiting for that write to land and reading its group counts on the CPU (OoT's culling: about 1.4 drains a frame of the whole ring); off by default

name: DM_VK_IP_READ
meaning: Android: `0` makes a dispatch that reads a storage buffer a draw wrote in place in a placed pool (raw global memory) wait for that chunk, as before; by default it reads the pool where the draw wrote, behind the dispatch's barrier (Ocarina of Time: two drains of the ring a frame)

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_STORE_WAIT
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `0` lets the replay's CPU reads of guest memory go on past a submission whose shaders stored through the raw pool table; by default such a submission counts as a write-back of unknown range until it completes, and the next read waits for it

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_SYNC
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `1` lands every pending write-back and large copy before each draw or dispatch that binds the raw pool table (the GPU reads guest memory when it runs, the write-backs land when their submission completes); by default such draws are only counted

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_TEST
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `1` runs a compute shader once the first raw pool table is built, which reads 16 bytes at 64 addresses in placed pools through the table and physical pointers, and logs whether the GPU's bytes match the CPU's

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_WRITTEN
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on and chunked placement (`DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_LAZY`): `1` also places the chunks the CPU wrote (a page present or swapped out), as before the pointer scan; by default a chunk only the CPU wrote stays unplaced, and a raw load from it reads 0

name: DM_VK_RAW_GMEM_WSYNC
meaning: Android, with raw global memory on: `1` makes each uniform buffer update, copy or fill the replay applies while recording, over a placed pool, wait for every submission still to run that bound the raw pool table (a raw load reads guest memory when the GPU runs it); by default only pages read in place by a storage buffer are waited for

name: DM_VK_RC_LANDED
meaning: Android, with the profile key `render_cond`: `0` keeps drawing under every condition on a samples-passed report, as before; by default such a condition reads the report's result once its submission has completed, and keeps drawing only while it is in flight (`dm/android/gfx_vk.c` `rc_value`)

name: DM_VK_RECORDER
meaning: Android: `1` makes the replay's vkCmd* calls, and each chunk's end and submission, on a thread of their own (`vk-record`, `gfx_vk_rec.inc`): the replay copies each call's arguments into a ring and waits for it only at the present; off by default, and on for Breath of the Wild and Ocarina of Time through their `android_defaults.txt`

name: DM_VK_REC_DESC
meaning: Android, with `DM_VK_RECORDER=1`: `0` writes descriptor sets on the replay thread (`vkUpdateDescriptorSets`), as before; by default the recorder thread makes the writes too, from a record queued ahead of the set's bind (`dm/android/gfx_vk_rec.inc` `R_UPDDS`, `rec_desc.h`)

name: DM_VK_REFUSE_SUBMIT
meaning: Android: `=<n>` refuses the nth queue submission with -3, as a Qualcomm driver refused one of Skyrim's (droidplay-core#444), to test that a refused submission doesn't stop the game: its fence goes alone and the chunk completes with its work dropped; `=-<n>` refuses the fence alone too, so the GPU counts as lost and the chunk completes without waiting on its fence (`gfx_vk.c` `submit_or_fence`)

name: DM_VK_RES_EXT
meaning: Android: `0` ignores the constant buffer extents in each shader's `res.json` (`tools/spv_android.py` `cb_extents`, which bound indices computed at run time, a loop's counter); on by default, taken where not below the SPIR-V scan's (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `cb_ext_pick`)

name: DM_VK_SAFE
meaning: Android: `1` turns off the replay's GPU forwarding, early submissions and window fences (every sync waits), to tell a sync bug from a drawing one

name: DM_VK_SB_CHECK
meaning: Android: `1` keeps a shadow of each read-only storage buffer copy `DM_VK_SB_DIRTY` makes, compares every bind the dirty-page tracker lets through with it, and logs (the first 8) and counts the ones that differ, copying them again (`dm/android/gfx_vk_sbcopy.inc`)

name: DM_VK_SB_DIRTY
meaning: Android: `0` compares a read-only storage buffer outside placed pools, which `sb_keep` does not keep, with a shadow of its chunk's copy at every bind, as before; by default the copy is stamped and its pages protected, and a later bind in the chunk takes it while the dirty-page tracker shows no page written since (`dm/android/gfx_vk_sbcopy.inc`)

name: DM_VK_SB_KEEP
meaning: Android: `0` copies a storage buffer a shader only reads into the arena in every chunk that reads it, as before; by default it is kept on the GPU between frames as geometry is, while the dirty-page tracker shows no write to it (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `sb_keep`)

name: DM_VK_SC_SRGB
meaning: Android: `0` keeps the swapchain in R8G8B8A8_UNORM for every frame; by default it is made in R8G8B8A8_SRGB while the presented window texture is sRGB, where the surface lists that format, so the front end's blit carries the frame's bytes instead of showing them decoded to linear, a gamma too dark (`front_android.c` `sc_encoding`)

name: DM_VK_SET_REUSE
meaning: Android: `1` makes constant buffers dynamic uniform buffers and binds again a descriptor set already written with the same descriptors in the chunk being recorded (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `sr_find`); off by default (every set written, as before)

name: DM_VK_SHADOW_RT
meaning: Android: `=<W>x<H>` or `=square<N>` (any square target of N or more): the shadow maps `DM_VK_SKIP_SHADOWS` looks for, in place of the profile's `vk_shadow_rt` (to find a game's; the log's `shadow map … set as the target` lines name the shapes caught)

name: DM_VK_SHARED_MAX
meaning: Android: `=<bytes>` the shared memory limit `spv_tgspill.h` moves compute shaders' shared memory past, in place of the GPU's `maxComputeSharedMemorySize`: a smaller one tries the move on a GPU with room

name: DM_VK_SKIP_SHADOWS
meaning: Android: `1` leaves out the draws of the game's shadow-map passes, depth-only passes on a target of the shape its profile's `vk_shadow_rt` names (`gfx_vk_shadow.inc`): no shadows and a cheaper frame, the game's own clears of the map kept; off by default, and it does nothing for a game whose profile names no shadow map

name: DM_VK_SLOT0_FILL
meaning: Android: a render pass with colour slot 0 empty below a used slot gets a scratch RGBA8 target in slot 0, and one whose colour slots are all empty is made with no colour slot (on by default on Qualcomm's own driver, by its Vulkan driver ID (driverVersion's top bit when the driver gives no ID), so not on Turnip: on the 830 such a pass left its target so that a later pass drawing into it hung the GPU, and on the 730 the pass's end crashed in the driver (Mario Kart 8 Deluxe; Divinity: Original Sin 2, a depth-stencil pass with one empty colour slot); `1` on any GPU, `0` off, both; `gfx_vk_draw.inc` `slot0_fill_on`)

name: DM_VK_STORAGE_UP
meaning: Android: a texture made without NVN's image flag and bound to an image slot all the same is made again with storage use (`gfx_vk.c` `vt_storage_up`). `0` binds it as it is, as before; `1` (default) upgrades one whose own format the GPU stores to and still skips an sRGB one (red line 125); `2` upgrades that too, storing through its UNORM twin (Ocarina of Time's title then runs its upscaler, which draws noise on the Adreno 830)

name: DM_VK_TBUF_ROWS
meaning: Android: `0` makes a buffer texture in a 2D texture slot read 0, as before; by default a slot the translator reads by wrapped 1D fetches (res.json `fetch1d`) or whose handle is in a uniform buffer gets an image of the buffer as rows of 16,384 texels, uploaded from guest memory and again when its pages change (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `tex_rows_slot`, `dm/android/tbuf_rows.h`; [Buffer textures read through a 2D slot, as rows on Vulkan](reference/rendering.md#buffer-textures-read-through-a-2d-slot-as-rows-on-vulkan-android))

name: DM_VK_THERMAL
meaning: Android: `0` reports no thermal state (as before); on by default, Android's thermal status (AThermal) feeds the frame step's thermal cap, which holds 30 fps from severe (`DM_THERMAL_CAP=0` turns only the cap off)

name: DM_VK_TF_FRAG
meaning: Android: `1` captures transform feedback in the fragment stage on any GPU with fragment-stage storage writes, to compare it with the vertex-stage capture on an Adreno; `0` never does, so a GPU without vertex-stage storage writes captures nothing (red line 115), as before. By default only such a GPU (Arm's Mali) captures in the fragment stage: each vertex a one-pixel point, its outputs stored by a fragment shader made at run time (`dm/android/spv_tffrag.h`)

name: DM_VK_UPSCALER_SQUARE
meaning: Android: `1` (Ocarina of Time's `android_defaults.txt`) replaces an upscaler network of agl's NDSR interface, square-root E5B9G9R9 colour in and a larger B10G11R11 image out, by a bilinear scale and a signed square (`gfx_vk_upsq.inc`); `0` runs the network as the game made it

name: DM_VK_UPSCALER_SQUARE_CS
meaning: Android: `<key>[,<key>...]`: compute shaders whose dispatches are replaced by a bilinear scale and a signed square besides those `DM_VK_UPSCALER_SQUARE` matches (`gfx_vk_upsq.inc`); `0` runs every network

name: DM_VK_VS_LAYERS
meaning: Android: `=<n>`: a vertex shader's layer reaches only layers 0 to n-1 of a layered pass, so a draw whose vertex shader writes the layer into more layers is made once per n layers, into views from the group's first layer (`gfx_vk_draw.inc` `vs_layer_groups`); `0`: every draw made once. 8 on Arm's Mali driver (the Mali-G715 drops a primitive whose layer from a vertex shader is 8 or more), 0 elsewhere

name: DM_VK_WB_READBACK
meaning: Android: `0` reads the arena's write-backs (storage buffers, buffer images, transform feedback) from the arena on the completion thread, as before; by default they are copied on the GPU into a cached transfer-destination buffer and read from there where the arena's memory type reads at under a third of that one's speed on the CPU (measured at start: the Retroid Pocket 5's driver maps its cached coherent type uncached), and `1` copies them wherever such a type exists (`gfx_vk_readback.inc`)

name: DM_VK_WB_WORDS
meaning: Android: `0` lands storage buffers' write-backs (and storage texel buffers') with the byte loop and every page of the buffer prepared, as before; by default the bytes the GPU changed against the snapshot are found a word at a time and only the span from the first to the last is prepared (`gfx_vk.c` `wb_apply`)

name: DM_VSYNC_HZ
meaning: `=<Hz>`: rate at which a host thread fires the vi vsync event when the display link does not drive it (default 60)

name: DM_WAKE_DEFER
meaning: `0` lets a thread woken or started by a higher-priority thread pinned to its core run at once, beside its waker; on by default, it waits until the waker gives the core up (a guest wait, a sleep, a file system call), at most 50 ms (`hle_thread.c` `wake_defer`)

name: DM_WATCH
meaning: `=<s>` dumps all threads after that many seconds (SIGALRM) and turns on the stall watchdog; off unless set

name: DM_WATCH_SAMPLE
meaning: `=<path>` (Mac): when the stall watchdog fires, samples the process for 1 s with `/usr/bin/sample` and writes the thread stacks to that path

name: DM_WATCH_STALL
meaning: `=<s>`: when the frame loop makes no progress for that long (default 15 with `DM_WATCH`), logs a red line, dumps the threads and exits

name: DM_WEB_LOG
meaning: `1` logs each key an offline HTML page is given and where the focus is after it

name: DM_WINDOW
meaning: When set (to any value, `0` included) opens a Mac window with keyboard and controller input; unset runs headless with the guest on the current thread; the Mac launcher sets it

name: DM_WINDOW_TOP
meaning: `1` (Mac, with `DM_WINDOW`) orders the game window in front without activating it and keeps it above other apps' windows, so a covered window does not slow the run; `regress.py` sets it

name: DM_XCODE_DERIVED_DATA
meaning: Xcode derived data folder for `build_ipa.sh` (default `$W/build/ios/xcode-dd`); the NSP script points it into the game's build folder

name: DM_XCODE_PROJECT_DIR
meaning: Folder of the per-game Xcode project that `build_ipa.sh --prepare-xcode` makes (default `$W/xcode`); the NSP script sets it

name: DM_XV_FILE
meaning: File where the attachment validity ledger keeps the keys it disabled after a violation, read at the next launch

name: DM_YIELD_BACKOFF
meaning: `0` turns off the yield back-off; `=<cap µs>[:<start µs>]` sets its sleep cap and the run of yields after which it starts (default 250:2000)

name: DM_YIELD_CLOCK
meaning: Clock-reading yield loops: 0 uses ordinary yield backoff, 1 backs off from the start, 2 also sleeps to the predicted end (default)
